lines: {target}? Black stone and lava leave little mercy.
If someone goes to Basalt Deltas, tell them this. Step like every block wants an argument.
Ash and basalt make the Nether feel broken twice.
I will remember Basalt Deltas as as jagged black country with heat in its cracks.
When the danger first showed itself near the basalt deltas, did you have room to back away?
If I followed your route to the basalt deltas, where would I be most likely to lose it?
Good footing is easy to miss until it disappears. Where did yours disappear?
I trust a route less when the sky changes. What was it like over the basalt deltas?
Did the lack of water become its own danger near the basalt deltas?
I know how to read a current. I am not sure I could read the basalt deltas.
Plain bread can feel like a feast after a place like the basalt deltas.
Show me the gear that took the worst of the basalt deltas. I want to see the marks.
Did stone between you and the fire hold until daylight?
Did the group argue before the danger or only after it passed?
Which sound from the basalt deltas still follows you into quiet rooms?
Could you avoid a fight, or had the danger already closed the way?
Did the marked route back to the portal feel harder once everyone was tired?
Did the journey change how you prepare for ordinary roads?
I know the look of someone remembering bad water. A trip to the basalt deltas can leave something similar.
If you went back, what would you pack before anything else?
{target}? Red Nether trees grow among hoglins and worse.
Anyone bound for Crimson Forest should hear this. Keep gold on and eyes open.
The whole forest looks like it has a pulse.
I'll remember Crimson Forest as a red forest that feels too alive.
Once lava and whatever followed the noise became a problem, could you still turn around?
Which landmark helped you remember the marked route back to the portal?
Where around the crimson forest did one careful step matter most?
Weather has ruined kinder roads than that. How did your supplies hold up?
A fisherman thinks about water even on dry ground. What water could you count on there?
My worst crossing sounds manageable beside what happened at the crimson forest.
What did you eat when the road near the crimson forest ran longer than planned?
How well did fire protection and a strong rope survive the trip to the crimson forest?
When you finally stopped near the crimson forest, what did you put between yourself and danger?
Would you trust the same people beside you at the crimson forest again?
What sound meant safety was finally close?
What kept the first bad encounter from becoming the last one?
What did you promise yourself while the marked route back to the portal stretched ahead?
What warning would you give before anyone else heads toward the crimson forest?
You do not have to make the crimson forest sound braver than it felt.
Does curiosity still point toward the crimson forest, or has good sense won?
{target}? The Nether wastes neither heat nor cruelty.
Before another traveler leaves for Nether Wastes, warn them. Watch ghasts, cliffs, and every pool of lava.
Netherrack crumbles like it enjoys the fall.
I'll remember Nether Wastes as red stone and fire with no decent sky.
Was the worst part of the nether wastes obvious, or did it wait until you were committed?
How much of the journey to the nether wastes depended on landmarks instead of a map?
How badly did hot stone and broken ledges slow you down?
Which came first near the nether wastes, the bad weather or the bad decision?
Did you carry enough clean water to cook near the nether wastes?
A boat has edges you can understand, while a trip to the nether wastes sounds less honest.
Was any food still dry when you finally stopped?
What broke first near the nether wastes, and how did you manage without it?
A dry bed changes the memory of a hard road. Did you find one?
If you returned to the nether wastes, whom would you ask to come along?
I judge weather by sound on the water. What sound guided you near the nether wastes?
Did putting distance behind you make the danger any easier to judge?
Did you save enough strength for the road home?
Someone will hear this and go anyway. What must they remember?
You look farther away when you speak about the nether wastes. Does it still feel close?
Could better weather ever persuade you to take that road again?
{target}? The ground pulls back when you try to leave.
Pass this along to whoever visits Soul Sand Valley. Wear good boots and keep ghasts in mind.
Soul sand makes every step feel watched.
I will remember Soul Sand Valley as a valley where the floor does not want guests.
What made you lower your voice when you reached the soul sand valley?
Did you mark the turns near the soul sand valley, or trust yourself to remember them?
I know what wet docks do to balance. What did hot stone and broken ledges do to yours?
What did heat and drifting ash do to your plans?
What would you have traded for a clean drink near the soul sand valley?
A leaking boat can be patched. I would not know where to start with the soul sand valley.
I hope somebody saved supper for the return from the soul sand valley.
How much of your gear came back needing repair?
Could anyone sleep near the soul sand valley, or did you keep watch until morning?
Did you have someone watching the way back while you watched ahead?
Tell me what the place sounded like at night. That usually reveals the truth.
At the soul sand valley, which threat made everyone change plans fastest?
Which familiar landmark finally let you breathe normally again?
What did the soul sand valley teach you that a map never could?
Did returning home settle the fear, or merely give it somewhere quiet to sit?
Would you return to the soul sand valley if someone you trusted asked?
{target}? Blue Nether trees make sense feel optional.
The next person heading toward Warped Forest needs your warning. Keep gold on and eyes off trouble.
Warped wood looks wrong even before it moves.
I will remember Warped Forest as a blue forest that forgot what forests are for.
Before things went wrong at the warped forest, what warning did everyone miss?
The path back matters more than the path in. What did you use to find it?
What sort of footing gave you the most trouble near the warped forest?
Could you see the way home once heat and drifting ash began?
What did you rely on for drinking water near the warped forest?
The dock will feel wonderfully ordinary after hearing that story.
What food would you carry twice as much of if you returned?
I would check every knot after that journey. What needs mending now?
Which place did you choose for camp, and what made you trust it?
Tell me you had steady company on that road.
Did the sounds around you make the danger seem closer than it was?
How much luck was left by the time you got clear?
How long did it take before the village felt close again?
What do people misunderstand most when they talk about the warped forest?
Some journeys stay in the hands after the road ends. Is this one of them?
Would you guide another traveler there, or only warn them away?
